title: Pakistan Studies MCQs: Independence & Early Challenges (1947-1958)

questions.question: On which date did Pakistan achieve independence?
questions.explanation: Pakistan was created as an independent dominion on 14 August 1947, while India became independent on 15 August 1947.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the founder of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, known as Quaid-e-Azam, founded Pakistan and served as its first Governor-General.

questions.question: When did India announce independence?
questions.explanation: India became independent on 15 August 1947, one day after Pakistan, under the Indian Independence Act.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Jinnah served as the first Governor-General of Pakistan from August 1947 until his death in September 1948.

questions.question: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam die?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Jinnah died on 11 September 1948, less than a year after independence.

questions.question: When was the British Indian Independence Act passed?
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in July 1947, formally authorizing the partition.

questions.question: Who was Pakistan's first Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan became Pakistan's first Prime Minister after the death of Quaid-e-Azam in 1948.

questions.question: When was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated on 16 October 1951 at a public rally in Company Bagh, Rawalpindi.

questions.question: Who assassinated Liaquat Ali Khan?
questions.explanation: Syed Akbar Khan, allegedly an Afghan national, shot Liaquat Ali Khan during a public meeting in Rawalpindi.

questions.question: Where was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated at Company Bagh (now renamed Liaquat Bagh) in Rawalpindi.

questions.question: When did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: Pakistan was admitted as a member of the United Nations on 30 September 1947.

questions.question: What was the capital of Pakistan at the time of independence?
questions.explanation: Karachi was the capital of Pakistan at independence. It remained the capital until 1959 when Rawalpindi became the interim capital.

questions.question: Approximately how many people migrated during the partition of 1947?
questions.explanation: Between 14 and 20 million people crossed borders during partition, making it one of the largest mass migrations in human history.

questions.question: How many articles did the 1956 Constitution contain?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution of Pakistan contained 234 articles and was a lengthy and detailed document.

questions.question: When was Pakistan's first constitution enforced?
questions.explanation: The Constitution of 1956 was enforced on 23 March 1956, making Pakistan an Islamic Republic.

questions.question: What did the 1956 Constitution declare Pakistan to be?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution declared Pakistan to be an Islamic Republic, establishing Islam as the foundation of governance.

questions.question: When was the Objectives Resolution passed?
questions.explanation: The Objectives Resolution was passed by the Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949, serving as the foundation for Pakistan's future constitution.

questions.question: Who presented the Objectives Resolution to the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan presented the Objectives Resolution to the Constituent Assembly in March 1949.

questions.question: In which constitution was the Objectives Resolution made a substantive part?
questions.explanation: The Objectives Resolution was made a substantive part of the Constitution through the Eighth Amendment to the 1973 Constitution.

questions.question: When was the One Unit scheme introduced?
questions.explanation: The One Unit scheme was introduced in 1955 to merge all provinces of West Pakistan into a single administrative unit.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the One Unit scheme?

options.B: To merge West Pakistani provinces into one administrative unit

questions.explanation: The One Unit scheme aimed to unite the four provinces of West Pakistan into a single administrative unit to streamline governance.

questions.question: Who was the second Governor-General of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second Governor-General of Pakistan after Jinnah's death.

questions.question: When did the 1947-48 Kashmir War occur?
questions.explanation: The Kashmir War began in October 1947 when tribal forces attacked Kashmir, and lasted until January 1949 when a ceasefire was agreed.

questions.question: What was the main issue of the Kashmir dispute?

options.C: The Maharaja's accession to India despite Muslim majority population

questions.explanation: The Kashmir dispute arose because the Hindu Maharaja of Kashmir chose to accede to India, despite the state having a Muslim majority population.

questions.question: Which UN Security Council resolution called for a ceasefire in Kashmir?
questions.explanation: UN Security Council Resolution 47 called for a ceasefire in Kashmir in 1948.

questions.question: Which princely state was integrated into Pakistan without much resistance?
questions.explanation: Kalat was relatively smoothly integrated into Pakistan compared to other princely states.

questions.question: Who was the ruler of Hyderabad who resisted accession?
questions.explanation: Mir Osman Ali Khan, the Nizam of Hyderabad, initially resisted accession to India, seeking independence.

questions.question: When did Hyderabad accede to India?
questions.explanation: Hyderabad was forced to accede to India in November 1948 after Operation Polo.

questions.question: Which princely state was located in the southwest of Gujarat and had a Muslim ruler?
questions.explanation: Junagadh was a princely state in southwestern Gujarat ruled by Mohammad Mahabat Khan and had a Muslim ruler.

questions.question: When did Junagadh accede to Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Junagadh's ruler acceded to Pakistan in September 1947, but India later occupied it and conducted a referendum.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the Junagadh referendum?

options.C: It acceded to India with overwhelming majority
options.D: It was divided between India and Pakistan

questions.explanation: The Junagadh referendum, conducted by India, resulted in an overwhelming majority voting for accession to India.

questions.question: Who was the Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir at the time of partition?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Hari Singh was the ruler of Jammu and Kashmir at partition, and he chose to accede to India.

questions.question: When did the Maharaja of Kashmir sign the Instrument of Accession with India?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession with India on 26 October 1947.

questions.question: Who was the first Prime Minister of India at the time of partition?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India at the time of partition.

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy during the partition of India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India and played a key role in the partition arrangements.

questions.question: On what date did Lord Mountbatten announce the Partition Plan?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten announced the partition plan on 3 June 1947, setting August 15 as independence day.

questions.question: Who was in charge of drawing the boundary between India and Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe was appointed to draw the boundary (Radcliffe Line) between India and Pakistan.

questions.question: When did Sir Cyril Radcliffe announce the Boundary Commission Award?
questions.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe announced the Boundary Commission Award on 17 August 1947.

questions.question: How many hours of notice was given for the Radcliffe Award announcement?
questions.explanation: The Radcliffe Award was announced with minimal notice, causing confusion and chaos.

questions.question: What is another name for the Radcliffe Line?
questions.explanation: The Radcliffe Line is the boundary drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe between India and Pakistan.

questions.question: Which two provinces did Pakistan consist of at independence?
questions.explanation: Pakistan consisted of West Pakistan and East Pakistan (now Bangladesh), separated by about 1000 miles of Indian territory.

questions.question: Which cities were included in West Pakistan at independence?
questions.explanation: West Pakistan included the provinces of Punjab, Sindh, NWFP, and Balochistan with major cities like Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar, and Quetta.

questions.question: What was the population of Pakistan at independence?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's population at independence in 1947 was approximately 30-35 million people.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the first Chief Justice of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Sir Abdul Rasheed was appointed as the first Chief Justice of Pakistan.

questions.question: When was the State Bank of Pakistan established?
questions.explanation: The State Bank of Pakistan was established on 1 July 1948.

questions.question: What was Liaquat Ali Khan's main focus during his tenure as Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan focused on consolidating the new nation, rehabilitating refugees, and establishing institutions.

questions.question: How many members were in Pakistan's first Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan had 79 members.

questions.question: What was the full name of the Basic Principles Committee?
questions.explanation: The Basic Principles Committee was established to formulate basic principles for the future constitution.

questions.question: How many Basic Principles Committee reports were submitted?
questions.explanation: Two major Basic Principles Committee reports were submitted (1950 and 1952) before the 1956 Constitution was finalized.

questions.question: What was a major challenge in Pakistan's early years?
questions.explanation: Pakistan faced multiple challenges including refugee rehabilitation, financial disputes with India, and military conflicts over Kashmir.

questions.question: How much did India agree to pay Pakistan as financial settlement?
questions.explanation: The financial settlement involved India agreeing to pay Pakistan 750 million rupees (approximately 55 crores).

questions.question: What was the main issue regarding canal waters between India and Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The canal water dispute was about irrigation rights and control of water flowing to Pakistan through canals built in India.

questions.question: Which rivers were the main subject of the canal water dispute?
questions.explanation: The main disputes were over the Indus and Sutlej rivers which were crucial for Pakistan's irrigation.

questions.question: When was the Indus Waters Treaty signed?
questions.explanation: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed on 19 September 1960, resolving the canal water dispute between India and Pakistan.

questions.question: How many military assets did Pakistan receive during partition?
questions.explanation: Pakistan inherited approximately one-third of the British Indian Army and its assets.

questions.question: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of Pakistan Army?
questions.explanation: General Frank Messervy was appointed as the first Commander-in-Chief of Pakistan Army.

questions.question: When was the first census of Pakistan conducted?
questions.explanation: The first census of Pakistan was conducted in 1951.

questions.question: What was the official language declared in the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution declared both Urdu and Bengali as national languages of Pakistan.

questions.question: When was Urdu officially declared as the national language?
questions.explanation: Urdu was officially declared as the national language of Pakistan in 1948.

questions.question: What was Pakistan's form of government under the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution established Pakistan as a federal parliamentary republic.

questions.question: How many parts did the 1956 Constitution have?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution was divided into 13 parts plus a preamble.

questions.question: Who was the first President of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Iskander Mirza was the first President of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution.

questions.question: What was the prescribed age for the President under the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution prescribed 55 years as the minimum age for the President.

questions.question: How many seats were there in the Senate under the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution provided for a Senate with 60 seats.

questions.question: What type of electoral system was provided in the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution initially provided for indirect elections through an Electoral College.

questions.question: How long was the 1956 Constitution enforced?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution was abrogated in 1958 after only 3 years, when the military took over.

questions.question: Which article of the 1956 Constitution dealt with Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Part II of the 1956 Constitution dealt with Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy.

questions.question: What was the condition for the President's religion in the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim.

questions.question: When did East Pakistan declare independence as Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: East Pakistan declared independence as Bangladesh in 1971 after the Bangladesh Liberation War.

questions.question: What was the composition of the Legislative Assembly under the 1956 Constitution?

options.B: Bicameral with Senate and National Assembly

questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution established a bicameral legislature with a Senate and National Assembly.

questions.question: How many members were in the National Assembly under the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The National Assembly under the 1956 Constitution had 210 members.

questions.question: Who presided over the Constituent Assembly that framed the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Bogra presided over the sessions that led to the completion of the 1956 Constitution.

questions.question: What was the first sentence of the 1956 Constitution's Preamble?

options.D: In the name of Allah, the Merciful

questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution's Preamble began with 'In the name of Allah' and included the Objectives Resolution.

questions.question: Which of the following was a feature of the 1956 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution featured a parliamentary system, declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic, and established a federal structure.

questions.question: When did the first 9 years of constitution-making deadlock period start?
questions.explanation: The constitution-making process began after independence in August 1947, lasting 9 years until 1956.

questions.question: Which province had the largest share of Muslims in West Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Punjab had the largest Muslim population among West Pakistani provinces at independence.

questions.question: What was the capital of East Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Dhaka was the capital of East Pakistan (now Bangladesh).

questions.question: Which countries recognized Pakistan first after independence?
questions.explanation: Britain recognized Pakistan almost immediately, followed by Middle Eastern countries including Egypt.

questions.question: When was Egypt the first country to recognize Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Egypt was among the first countries to recognize Pakistan on 16 August 1947.

questions.question: How many provinces did Pakistan have at independence?
questions.explanation: Pakistan had 4 provinces: Punjab, Sindh, NWFP, and Balochistan in West Pakistan, plus East Pakistan.

questions.question: When was the first Governor of Pakistan appointed?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was appointed as the first Governor-General in August 1947.

questions.question: What was the condition for Pakistan's independence under the Independence Act?

options.A: Pakistan had to accept British sovereignty
options.B: Pakistan became a Dominion within the British Commonwealth
options.C: Pakistan had to have a British viceroy

questions.explanation: Pakistan became an independent dominion within the British Commonwealth of Nations.

questions.question: When did Pakistan leave the British Commonwealth?
questions.explanation: Pakistan left the British Commonwealth in 1972 during the Bangladesh crisis.

questions.question: What was the total area of Pakistan at independence?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's total area at independence was approximately 876,000 square miles.

questions.question: Who led the refugees after partition from West Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Refugees who migrated to Pakistan were called 'Muhajirs' (migrants or refugees).

questions.question: How many refugees came to Pakistan during partition?
questions.explanation: Approximately 7-10 million refugees migrated to Pakistan during and immediately after partition.

questions.question: What was the main challenge for Pakistan regarding refugee rehabilitation?
questions.explanation: Pakistan faced severe challenges in housing, employment, and food supply for millions of refugees.

questions.question: When was the Ministry of Refugees and Rehabilitation established in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Refugees and Rehabilitation was established immediately after independence to manage the refugee crisis.

questions.question: Which city was the center of refugee settlement in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Karachi became the main center for refugee settlement due to its port facilities and accessibility.

questions.question: When was the last major wave of refugees settled in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Refugee migration and settlement continued until around 1950, with minor migrations even later.

questions.question: What percentage of Pakistan's population consisted of refugees?
questions.explanation: Refugees constituted about 25-35% of Pakistan's population at independence.

questions.question: Who was the first Muslim League President from East Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy was a prominent politician from East Pakistan.

questions.question: When was the Defense of India Act of 1915 extended to Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Pakistan adopted its own legislation, not directly extending British laws wholesale.

questions.question: What was Pakistan's initial monetary policy?
questions.explanation: Pakistan introduced its own currency, the Pakistan rupee, as a symbol of independence.

questions.question: When was the Pakistan rupee formally introduced?
questions.explanation: The Pakistan rupee was introduced in September 1947, within weeks of independence.

questions.question: What was the relation between Pakistan and Britain after 1947?
questions.explanation: Pakistan became an independent dominion with equal status to other Commonwealth nations.

questions.question: When was the Simla Agreement signed between India and Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Simla Agreement was signed on 19 July 1949, establishing ceasefire line in Kashmir.

questions.question: What did the Simla Agreement establish?
questions.explanation: The Simla Agreement established the ceasefire line (now called Line of Control) in Kashmir.

questions.question: Who signed the Simla Agreement for Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan, as Prime Minister, was involved in negotiations for the Simla Agreement.

questions.question: When was the first General Elections planned in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The first General Elections in Pakistan were held in 1956 under the new constitution.

questions.question: What was the status of Islam in the Objectives Resolution?
questions.explanation: The Objectives Resolution established Islam as the spiritual and moral foundation of the Pakistani state.

questions.question: What did the Objectives Resolution guarantee for minorities?
questions.explanation: The Objectives Resolution guaranteed religious freedom and adequate representation for minorities.

questions.question: When was the first Constituent Assembly dissolved?
questions.explanation: The first Constituent Assembly was dissolved in 1954, replaced by a second assembly.

questions.question: Who dissolved the first Constituent Assembly in 1954?
questions.explanation: Governor-General Muhammad Ali Jinnah's successor dissolved the assembly in 1954.

questions.question: How many times was the Constituent Assembly reconstituted?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly was reconstituted twice - once in 1954 - before finalizing the constitution in 1956.

questions.question: What was the main political controversy in the early years of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Pakistan faced multiple controversies including the Urdu vs Bengali language dispute, federalism issues, and religious interpretation.

questions.question: When did the Bengali Language Movement start?
questions.explanation: The Bengali Language Movement reached its peak in 1952 when students protested against the imposition of Urdu.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the Bengali Language Movement of 1952?

options.D: English was chosen as official language

questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution eventually recognized both Urdu and Bengali as official languages.

questions.question: Who was the Governor-General after Muhammad Ali Jinnah?
questions.explanation: Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second Governor-General after Jinnah's death.

questions.question: When did Khawaja Nazimuddin become Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Khawaja Nazimuddin was appointed Governor-General on 14 December 1948.

questions.question: Who became Prime Minister after Liaquat Ali Khan's assassination?
questions.explanation: Khawaja Nazimuddin became Prime Minister after Liaquat Ali Khan's death in 1951.

questions.question: When was Muhammad Ali Bogra appointed Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Bogra became Prime Minister in April 1953.

questions.question: What was Muhammad Ali Bogra's significant contribution?

options.A: Bogra Formula on confederation with India

questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Bogra presented the Constitutional Formula (Bogra Formula) which became the basis for the 1956 Constitution.

questions.question: When was the Bogra Formula presented?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Bogra presented his constitutional formula in September 1953.

questions.question: What was the significance of the Bogra Formula?

options.B: It paved the way for the 1956 Constitution

questions.explanation: The Bogra Formula addressed key constitutional issues and was instrumental in finalizing the 1956 Constitution.

questions.question: When did Muhammad Ali Bogra resign as Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Bogra resigned as Prime Minister in 1956 after the constitution was enacted.

questions.question: What was the 'Bait-ul-Maal' system in early Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Bait-ul-Maal system was an Islamic institution for welfare and support of the poor and needy.

questions.question: When were the first elections held in any province of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The first elections in Pakistan were held in Punjab in 1951.

questions.question: When were provincial elections held for the first time?
questions.explanation: The first provincial elections in Pakistan were held in December 1954.

questions.question: What was the major issue in the provincial elections of 1954?
questions.explanation: The 1954 provincial elections were significantly influenced by anti-Ahmadiyya agitation.

questions.question: What was the Rawalpindi Conspiracy?
questions.explanation: The Rawalpindi Conspiracy was a military plot discovered in 1951 to overthrow the government.

questions.question: When was the Rawalpindi Conspiracy discovered?
questions.explanation: The Rawalpindi Conspiracy was discovered in 1951.

questions.question: Who were the main conspirators in the Rawalpindi Conspiracy?
questions.explanation: The conspiracy involved military officers and alleged communist sympathizers.

questions.question: What was the punishment for the conspirators?
questions.explanation: The conspirators were imprisoned, though some were later pardoned.

questions.question: When was the Constituent Assembly inaugurated?
questions.explanation: The first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan was inaugurated on 14 August 1947.

questions.question: What was the first major issue debated in the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The nature of the state - whether it should be theocratic or secular - was the first major debate.

questions.question: Who were the founding fathers of Pakistan's constitution?
questions.explanation: The constitution was framed by multiple members of the Constituent Assembly, not by a single person.

questions.question: What was the role of the Governor-General in early Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Governor-General had significant executive and legislative powers in early Pakistan.

questions.question: When was the Emergency proclaimed in 1958?
questions.explanation: On 12 August 1958, Governor-General Iskander Mirza proclaimed Emergency, leading to military rule.

questions.question: Who took over the government in 1958?
questions.explanation: General Muhammad Ayub Khan took over the government on 27 September 1958.

questions.question: What happened to the 1956 Constitution in 1958?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution was abrogated when the military took over in 1958.

questions.question: How long did the 1956 Constitution remain in effect?
questions.explanation: The 1956 Constitution was in effect for about 2 years and 5 months until it was abrogated in 1958.

questions.question: What percentage of the population was urbanized in 1947?
questions.explanation: About 15% of Pakistan's population was urbanized at the time of independence.

questions.question: What was the literacy rate in Pakistan at independence?
questions.explanation: Pakistan had a low literacy rate of around 10% at the time of independence.

questions.question: When were the first educational reforms initiated in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Educational reforms were initiated immediately after independence in 1947.

questions.question: What was the main goal of early educational policy?
questions.explanation: Early educational policy focused on literacy and nation-building to create an informed citizenry.

questions.question: When was the All-Pakistan Muslim League Conference held?
questions.explanation: The All-Pakistan Muslim League Conference was held in 1953.

questions.question: What was Pakistan's initial foreign policy?
questions.explanation: Pakistan initially aligned with the Western bloc, joining SEATO and CENTO.

questions.question: When did Pakistan join SEATO?
questions.explanation: Pakistan joined SEATO (Southeast Asia Treaty Organization) in 1954.

questions.question: When did Pakistan join CENTO?
questions.explanation: Pakistan joined CENTO (Central Treaty Organization) in 1955.

questions.question: What was the economic policy of early Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Pakistan adopted a mixed economic system with both public and private sectors.

questions.question: When was the first Five-Year Plan launched?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1950.

questions.question: What was the focus of the first Five-Year Plan?
questions.explanation: The first Five-Year Plan focused on rehabilitation of refugees and basic infrastructure.

questions.question: When was Karachi University established?
questions.explanation: Karachi University was established in 1948 as Pakistan's first university.

questions.question: When was the first national flag of Pakistan designed?
questions.explanation: The national flag of Pakistan was adopted immediately after independence in August 1947.

questions.question: Who designed the flag of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The flag design was created and finalized by the national leaders including Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

questions.question: What do the colors of the Pakistani flag represent?

options.A: Green for Islam, White for minorities
options.B: Green for hope, White for peace
options.C: Green for nation, White for state
options.D: Green for land, White for water

questions.explanation: The green color represents Islam and the white represents minorities and peace.

questions.question: When was the national emblem of Pakistan finalized?
questions.explanation: The national emblem was finalized shortly after independence.

questions.question: What is the national flower of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Jasmine (Yasmeen) is the national flower of Pakistan.

questions.question: What is the national animal of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Markhor (a wild goat) is the national animal of Pakistan.

questions.question: When was the national anthem of Pakistan adopted?
questions.explanation: The national anthem was officially adopted in 1950.

questions.question: Who composed the national anthem of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Ahmed Ghazali Chagla composed the music for Pakistan's national anthem.

questions.question: When was the national poet of Pakistan declared?
questions.explanation: Allama Iqbal was declared the national poet (Poet of the East) before independence.

questions.question: When did Allama Iqbal die?
questions.explanation: Allama Iqbal died in 1938, before Pakistan's independence.

questions.question: What was Allama Iqbal's main contribution to Pakistan Movement?
questions.explanation: Allama Iqbal's main contribution was conceptualizing and popularizing the Two-Nation Theory.

questions.question: When did the idea of Pakistan as an independent state emerge?
questions.explanation: The Pakistan Movement crystallized with the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

questions.question: When was Liaquat Ali Khan elected as President of Muslim League?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was elected President of the Muslim League in 1945.

questions.question: What was the relationship between Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Liaquat Ali Khan?
questions.explanation: Jinnah mentored Liaquat Ali Khan, who served as his right-hand man.

questions.question: How many hours after Quaid-e-Azam's death did the Constituent Assembly meet?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly met within 24 hours of Jinnah's death to mourn and reorganize.

questions.question: What was the immediate response of the Assembly to Jinnah's death?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly continued its work under new leadership after Jinnah's death.

questions.question: When was the Constitution of 1956 finally drafted?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was finalized in January 1956 and enacted on 23 March 1956.

questions.question: Who was the first Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan was the first Speaker of the National Assembly.

questions.question: When did Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan become Speaker?
questions.explanation: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan was elected Speaker in August 1947.

questions.question: What was the tenure of the first Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The first Constituent Assembly served from 1947 to 1954.

questions.question: Who was elected President of the second Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: Hasrat Mohani was elected as President of the second Constituent Assembly.

questions.question: When was the second Constituent Assembly inaugurated?
questions.explanation: The second Constituent Assembly was inaugurated in June 1954.

questions.question: How many members were in the second Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The second Constituent Assembly had approximately 80 members.

questions.question: What was the main achievement of the second Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The second assembly successfully drafted the 1956 Constitution, addressing multiple constitutional issues.

questions.question: Who was Begum Jahanara Abdullab?
questions.explanation: Begum Jahanara Abdullab was Muhammad Ali Jinnah's sister who helped in social work.

questions.question: When was Begum Liaquat Ali Khan appointed as Governor of Sindh?
questions.explanation: Begum Liaquat Ali Khan was not appointed as Governor, though she was active in social work.

questions.question: What was Pakistan's initial foreign exchange reserves?
questions.explanation: Pakistan inherited limited foreign exchange reserves of approximately 200 million rupees.

questions.question: Who was the first Inspector General of Police of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Colonel Richard Bakewell was appointed as the first Inspector General of Police.

questions.question: When was the Federal Public Service Commission established?
questions.explanation: The Federal Public Service Commission was established in 1947.

questions.question: What were the main functions of the early FPSC?
questions.explanation: The FPSC was responsible for recruiting and selecting civil servants through competitive examinations.

questions.question: When was the first civil service examination held?
questions.explanation: The first Pakistan Civil Service examination was held in 1948.

questions.question: What was the Islamic nature of Pakistan as envisioned by Jinnah?
questions.explanation: Jinnah envisioned Pakistan as an Islamic state with democratic principles.

questions.question: What did Jinnah mean by 'Islam is our Faith, and State is our Nation'?
questions.explanation: Jinnah meant that Islam should be the foundation of the state's identity and principles.

questions.question: When did Jinnah address the Constituent Assembly on religious minorities?
questions.explanation: Jinnah made his famous speech on August 11, 1947 to the Constituent Assembly.

questions.question: What was Jinnah's position on the role of minorities in Pakistan?

options.C: They have equal rights as citizens

questions.explanation: Jinnah advocated for equal rights and protection for religious minorities in Pakistan.

questions.question: When did the Partition violence reach its peak?
questions.explanation: The partition violence was most severe in September-October 1947.

questions.question: Which cities witnessed the worst partition violence?
questions.explanation: Severe communal violence occurred in Punjab cities, Bengal, and Delhi.

questions.question: What was the estimated death toll from partition violence?
questions.explanation: Estimates of deaths during partition range from 1 to 2 million people.

questions.question: When did the basic reconciliation between India and Pakistan occur?
questions.explanation: While diplomatic relations were established, full reconciliation has never been achieved.

questions.question: What was Pakistan's strategy regarding princely states?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's strategy was to persuade princely states to accede through negotiation.

questions.question: Who was Pakistan's first Finance Minister?
questions.explanation: Ghulam Muhammad served as Pakistan's first Finance Minister.

questions.question: When was the State Bank Act passed?
questions.explanation: The State Bank Act was passed in 1948.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Abdur Rahman Khan was appointed as the first Governor of the State Bank.

questions.question: What was the main source of Pakistan's income in early years?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's economy was primarily based on agriculture in the early years.

questions.question: When was East Pakistan University (now University of Dhaka) established in West?
questions.explanation: The University of Dhaka was established before partition as a British Indian university.

questions.question: What was Liaquat Ali Khan's last public address about?
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan's last address focused on national unity and nation-building.

questions.question: How did the international community respond to Pakistan's creation?
questions.explanation: The international community generally welcomed Pakistan as a new nation.

questions.question: When was the Indo-Pakistan treaty on trade signed?

questions.question: What was Pakistan's population growth rate in the early years?

questions.question: What was the constitutional status of Pakistan until 1956?
questions.explanation: Pakistan was a Dominion within the British Commonwealth until 1956.

questions.explanation: The first cabinet reshuffle occurred after Jinnah's death in 1948.

questions.question: What was the major constitutional controversy of 1950?
questions.explanation: There were constitutional disputes over the Governor-General's powers in 1950.

questions.question: When was the Pakistan Penal Code adopted?
questions.explanation: Pakistan initially adopted the British Indian Penal Code and later modified it.

questions.question: What legacy did the 1947-1958 period leave for Pakistan?
questions.explanation: This period set patterns of constitutional instability and eventual military intervention in 1958.
